memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "But the fat portions of the ox and the ram—the fat tail, the layer of fat, the kidneys and the long lobe of the liver—these they laid on the breasts, and then Aaron burned the fat on the altar." - Lev 9:19-20 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The best portions go to God. We have read this instruction repeatedly through Leviticus; here it is finally being carried out.

There is a difference between knowing a principle and doing it. Aaron had heard these instructions. Now, with the whole nation watching, he actually placed the choicest parts on the fire where they would be lost to everyone.

That gap between knowing and doing is where most of the Christian life is decided.

We know we should forgive. We know we should give generously. We know we should speak the truth kindly, control our tongues, put God first in our schedules and our finances. Knowing costs nothing.

James addressed exactly this: Do not merely listen to the word, and so deceive yourselves. Do what it says (Jas 1:22). And he calls the alternative self-deception, which is a striking word. The person who hears and does not act genuinely believes they are further along than they are.

What do you know that you have never actually done?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What biblical principle do I understand well but have never actually put into practice?
2. What is one specific action I could take this week to close that gap?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, forgive me for knowing much and doing little. Move me from understanding to obedience today. Amen.
